column1: # Public-domain training corpus, one work per line:
#   form <TAB> gutenberg-id <TAB> slug <TAB> expected title substring
# `form` is what the model is taught to call this kind of text, and
# becomes the `form=` field of every instruction example built from it
# The expected-title column is a safety check, not decoration: a wrong
# Gutenberg id doesn't 404, it silently fetches a different book. fetch.sh
# reads the Title: line and skips anything that doesn't match, so a bad id
# costs one missing work rather than a corpus quietly full of the wrong
# A note on `screenplay`: film scripts are, almost without exception, not
# public domain, so what stands in for them here is public-domain drama —
# stage plays, in the same character-cue-and-dialogue shape a screenplay
# uses. That teaches the structure (who speaks, stage direction, scene
# breaks) even though it isn't film formatting. To train on actual film
# scripts, add them as sources in the app and fine-tune; that path is
# still there and is what it's for.
# Adding a work: append a line. Nothing else needs to change.
